## Bing: first main organic results

On the [Bing results page for “Latent Growth Models”](https://www.bing.com/search?q=Latent+Growth+Models), the top three main organic web results were, in order:

| Title | Source site | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| [Latent growth modeling - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latent_growth_modeling) | Wikipedia | An introduction to growth trajectories within structural equation modeling, including individual differences and model extensions. |
| [Estimating and visualizing Latent Growth Models with R](https://longitudinalanalysis.com/estimating-and-visualizing-latent-growth-models-with-r/) | Longitudinal Analysis | A practical tutorial on estimating growth models with lavaan and visualizing change using R. |
| [Latent Growth Model - an overview \| ScienceDirect Topics](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/psychology/latent-growth-model) | ScienceDirect | A topic overview collecting relevant chapter and article excerpts; its opening definition is explicitly labeled AI-generated. |

I excluded image/video blocks and Wikipedia’s supplementary links. **The Bing search page and all three source pages are open in separate tabs.**

## Reusable outline prompt

Using Google, I found Prompt Architects’ [ChatGPT Prompt Templates PDF](https://prompt-architects.com/blog/107-chatgpt-prompt-templates-pdf-free-download-2026) page. Its **“Fix the structure of a rambling draft”** template is useful for organizing existing material while preserving its wording and identifying missing information. The full template is visible on the page, which I left open.

Exact template text:

```text
FILL IN
  DRAFT     = [paste it]
  GOAL      = [what the reader should do or believe at the end]
  FORMAT    = [essay / doc / email / deck notes]
  CONSTRAINT= [anything that must stay in place, e.g. opening line]

Role: A structural editor who reorders before rewriting.
Task: Restructure DRAFT to serve GOAL.
Rules:
- Do not rewrite sentences yet. Move and label them.
- Identify anything that is said twice and mark the better version.
- Identify anything the reader needs that is missing. Mark it as a gap, do not
  fill it with invented content.
- Respect CONSTRAINT.
Output: The proposed outline with each existing paragraph mapped to a position,
a list of duplicates, and a list of gaps.

If any slot above is still in brackets, ask me for it. Do not guess it.
```

For your workflow, paste labeled source excerpts into `DRAFT`, set `FORMAT` to “study note,” and specify that source attributions must be preserved in `CONSTRAINT`.

## Bionic-style note — converter limitation

I entered your exact note into the [10015.io Bionic Reading Converter](https://10015.io/tools/bionic-reading-converter), but an advertisement overlay blocked further interaction. **I could not verify a converted result or leave a successful result visible as proof.** The converter tab remains open.

Here is a **manually formatted bionic-style version**, not a verified export from the converter:

> **Lat**ent **gro**wth **mod**els **ar**e **statis**tical **meth**ods **us**ed **t**o **esti**mate **cha**nge **ov**er **ti**me **acr**oss **indivi**duals. **Th**ey **he**lp **resear**chers **under**stand **trajec**tories, **differ**ences **i**n **gro**wth, **an**d **predi**ctors **o**f **cha**nge.

## Originality check before sharing

I finished with a Bing search and opened the actual [Quetext plagiarism checker](https://www.quetext.com/plagiarism-checker). Its live page displays a text-entry area, a **“Scan for plagiarism”** button, and an offer to check **1,000 words free**, with “No sign up required*.” That allowance is sufficient for your short note.

To use it:
- Paste your original plain-text note into **“Enter your text here.”**
- Click **“Scan for plagiarism”** and follow any verification prompts.
- Review the matched passages and linked sources; add citations or revise overly close wording before sharing.

I left the checker and its Bing search page open. I did **not** run a scan. Treat any similarity report as a review aid—not proof of originality—and cite the sources you used even if no matches appear.
